“Adventist” usually refers to Seventh-day Adventists, while “Baptist” covers a wide range of churches and associations. Both are Protestant Christian traditions that emphasize the Bible, salvation through Jesus Christ, and believers’ baptism by immersion.

- **Day of worship:** Seventh-day Adventists observe the Sabbath from Friday sunset to Saturday sunset. Most Baptists worship on Sunday.
- **Second Coming:** Both expect Christ’s return; Adventists give it a particularly prominent place in their teaching and identity.
- **Death and judgment:** Adventists generally teach that the dead remain unconscious until resurrection and that the wicked will ultimately be destroyed. Baptist beliefs vary, though many teach conscious existence after death and eternal punishment.
- **Health practices:** Adventists often emphasize dietary choices, including vegetarianism and abstaining from alcohol and tobacco. Baptists have no denomination-wide dietary rules, although some encourage abstinence from alcohol.
- **Church organization:** Seventh-day Adventists belong to a worldwide denomination with a structured leadership system. Baptist churches are typically autonomous and may affiliate with regional or national associations.
- **Ellen G. White:** Adventists regard her writings as a prophetic gift that guides the church, while holding the Bible as their highest authority. Baptists do not accept her as a prophet.

Practices can vary, so you could ask [local Adventist church] and [local Baptist church] about their beliefs and services in [location].

# ਸੌਫ਼ਟਵੇਅਰ ਇੰਜੀਨੀਅਰ ਦੇ ਤਕਨੀਕੀ ਹੁਨਰਾਂ ਦਾ ਮੁਲਾਂਕਣ

ਹਰੇਕ ਖੇਤਰ ਨੂੰ ਹੇਠਾਂ ਦਿੱਤੇ ਪੱਧਰਾਂ ਅਨੁਸਾਰ ਅੰਕ ਦਿਓ:

- **ਇੱਕ — ਸ਼ੁਰੂਆਤੀ:** ਬੁਨਿਆਦੀ ਸਮਝ ਸੀਮਤ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਲਗਾਤਾਰ ਮਦਦ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਹੈ।
- **ਦੋ — ਵਿਕਾਸਸ਼ੀਲ:** ਸਧਾਰਨ ਕੰਮ ਕਰ ਲੈਂਦਾ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਜਟਿਲ ਸਮੱਸਿਆਵਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਮਾਰਗਦਰਸ਼ਨ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਹੈ।
- **ਤਿੰਨ — ਸਮਰੱਥ:** ਆਮ ਕੰਮ ਸੁਤੰਤਰਤਾ ਨਾਲ ਅਤੇ ਭਰੋਸੇਯੋਗ ਢੰਗ ਨਾਲ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।
- **ਚਾਰ — ਨਿਪੁੰਨ:** ਜਟਿਲ ਕੰਮ ਪ੍ਰਭਾਵਸ਼ਾਲੀ ਢੰਗ ਨਾਲ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਆਪਣੇ ਫ਼ੈਸਲਿਆਂ ਦੇ ਕਾਰਨ ਸਮਝਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
- **ਪੰਜ — ਮਾਹਰ:** ਅਸਪਸ਼ਟ ਅਤੇ ਵੱਡੇ ਪੱਧਰ ਦੀਆਂ ਸਮੱਸਿਆਵਾਂ ਹੱਲ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਦੂਜਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਤਕਨੀਕੀ ਸਮਰੱਥਾ ਵਧਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

| ਮੁਲਾਂਕਣ ਦਾ ਖੇਤਰ | ਕੀ ਵੇਖਣਾ ਹੈ | ਭਾਰ |
|---|---|---:|
| ਸਮੱਸਿਆ ਹੱਲ ਕਰਨਾ | ਸਮੱਸਿਆ ਨੂੰ ਸਮਝਣਾ, ਭਾਗਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੰਡਣਾ, ਵਿਕਲਪਾਂ ਦੀ ਤੁਲਨਾ ਕਰਨਾ ਅਤੇ ਹੱਲ ਦੀ ਪੁਸ਼ਟੀ ਕਰਨਾ | ਵੀਹ ਫ਼ੀਸਦੀ |
| ਪ੍ਰੋਗਰਾਮ ਲਿਖਣਾ | ਸਹੀ, ਪੜ੍ਹਨਯੋਗ ਅਤੇ ਸੰਭਾਲਣਯੋਗ ਪ੍ਰੋਗਰਾਮ ਲਿਖਣਾ; ਭਾਸ਼ਾ ਦੀਆਂ ਬੁਨਿਆਦੀ ਵਿਸ਼ੇਸ਼ਤਾਵਾਂ ਦੀ ਵਰਤੋਂ | ਵੀਹ ਫ਼ੀਸਦੀ |
| ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ ਦੀ ਬਣਤਰ | ਲੋੜਾਂ ਅਨੁਸਾਰ ਭਾਗਾਂ ਦੀ ਬਣਤਰ, ਵਧਦੇ ਵਰਤੋਂਕਾਰਾਂ ਦਾ ਧਿਆਨ ਅਤੇ ਚੋਣਾਂ ਦੇ ਪ੍ਰਭਾਵ ਸਮਝਣਾ | ਪੰਦਰਾਂ ਫ਼ੀਸਦੀ |
| ਜਾਂਚ ਅਤੇ ਗੁਣਵੱਤਾ | ਢੁਕਵੀਆਂ ਜਾਂਚਾਂ ਲਿਖਣਾ, ਕਿਨਾਰੇ ਵਾਲੀਆਂ ਸਥਿਤੀਆਂ ਪਛਾਣਨਾ ਅਤੇ ਨਤੀਜਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਪੁਸ਼ਟੀ ਕਰਨਾ | ਪੰਦਰਾਂ ਫ਼ੀਸਦੀ |
| ਗ਼ਲਤੀਆਂ ਲੱਭਣਾ ਅਤੇ ਠੀਕ ਕਰਨਾ | ਲੱਛਣਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਮੂਲ ਕਾਰਨ ਤੱਕ ਪਹੁੰਚਣਾ, ਸਬੂਤ ਵਰਤਣਾ ਅਤੇ ਸੁਧਾਰ ਦੀ ਪੁਸ਼ਟੀ ਕਰਨਾ | ਦਸ ਫ਼ੀਸਦੀ |
| ਸੁਰੱਖਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਭਰੋਸੇਯੋਗਤਾ | ਜਾਣਕਾਰੀ ਦੀ ਸੁਰੱਖਿਆ, ਅਸਫਲਤਾਵਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਨਜਿੱਠਣਾ ਅਤੇ ਸੰਭਾਵੀ ਖ਼ਤਰਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਪਛਾਣਨਾ | ਦਸ ਫ਼ੀਸਦੀ |
| ਤਕਨੀਕੀ ਸੰਚਾਰ | ਆਪਣੇ ਤਰੀਕੇ, ਧਾਰਨਾਵਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਫ਼ੈਸਲਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਸਪਸ਼ਟ ਕਰਨਾ ਅਤੇ ਸੁਝਾਅ ਸਵੀਕਾਰ ਕਰਨਾ | ਦਸ ਫ਼ੀਸਦੀ |

ਮੁਲਾਂਕਣ ਲਈ ਇੱਕ ਵਿਹਾਰਕ ਕੰਮ, ਪ੍ਰੋਗਰਾਮ ਦੀ ਸਮੀਖਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਤਕਨੀਕੀ ਗੱਲਬਾਤ ਵਰਤੋ। ਹਰ ਖੇਤਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਅੰਕ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਦੇਖੇ ਗਏ ਕੰਮ ਦੀ ਇੱਕ ਠੋਸ ਉਦਾਹਰਨ ਦਰਜ ਕਰੋ। ਅੰਤਿਮ ਨਤੀਜਾ ਕੱਢਣ ਲਈ ਹਰ ਖੇਤਰ ਦੇ ਅੰਕ ਨੂੰ ਉਸ ਦੇ ਭਾਰ ਨਾਲ ਗੁਣਾ ਕਰਕੇ ਜੋੜੋ। ਭੂਮਿਕਾ ਦੇ ਤਜਰਬੇ ਦੇ ਪੱਧਰ ਅਤੇ ਕੰਮ ਦੀਆਂ ਲੋੜਾਂ ਅਨੁਸਾਰ ਉਮੀਦਾਂ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਤੈਅ ਕਰੋ।

**mara ellis**

glass artist and designer  
adelaide, south australia  
mara.ellis@example.com  
portfolio: maraellis.example.com  
phone: 0400 555 018

**professional profile**

i am an adelaide-based glass artist whose work explores light, memory, landscape and the changing relationship between built environments and the natural world. over the past twelve years, i have developed a practice that combines kiln-formed glass, glass blowing, cold working and mixed-media installation. my work ranges from intimate vessels and wall pieces to large-scale commissions for public and commercial spaces.

i am particularly interested in the translucent colours of the south australian coast and the subtle shifts in light across dry landscapes. i use layered glass, cast textures and polished surfaces to create objects that change in appearance throughout the day. my approach is grounded in careful material testing, collaborative design and a commitment to producing durable work that responds thoughtfully to its setting.

i have exhibited in artist-run spaces, regional galleries and group exhibitions across australia. alongside my studio practice, i teach introductory and intermediate glass workshops, mentor emerging artists and collaborate with architects, fabricators and community organisations. i am comfortable managing projects from an initial concept and budget through fabrication, installation and documentation.

**core skills**

- kiln forming, including fusing, slumping, casting and pâte de verre
- glass blowing and hot-shop assistance
- cold working, including cutting, grinding, polishing, drilling and sandblasting
- mould making with plaster, silica and refractory materials
- colour testing, sample development and material research
- concept development, sketching and three-dimensional prototyping
- public art proposals, budgets, schedules and installation plans
- collaboration with architects, interior designers and specialist fabricators
- workshop facilitation for adults, young people and community groups
- safe operation and maintenance of kilns, grinders and studio equipment
- artwork photography, exhibition documentation and portfolio preparation
- grant writing, artist statements and professional presentations

**professional experience**

**independent glass artist and designer**  
adelaide, south australia  
2014–present

develop and produce original glass artworks for exhibitions, private collections, architectural settings and public spaces. manage all stages of the creative process, from research and concept drawings to fabrication, finishing, packaging and delivery.

create small production runs of vessels and sculptural objects while maintaining a parallel practice focused on one-of-a-kind works. experiment with colour combinations, surface treatments and mould materials to achieve specific visual and structural outcomes.

work directly with clients to clarify project goals, identify installation requirements and establish realistic budgets. prepare samples and visual presentations so that clients can understand how a proposed piece will interact with its surroundings.

selected achievements:

- completed more than thirty commissions for homes, offices, hospitality venues and community spaces.
- developed a series of layered glass panels inspired by the changing colours of the gulf st vincent coastline.
- introduced a studio system for tracking firing schedules, material tests and finishing methods, improving consistency across complex projects.
- established relationships with local metalworkers and timber fabricators to support secure mounting and installation.
- presented artist talks and demonstrations for galleries, schools and community arts groups.

**glass workshop facilitator**  
southern light arts collective, adelaide  
2018–present

design and deliver practical workshops that introduce participants to glass cutting, composition, kiln forming and cold-working techniques. adapt sessions for beginners, returning students and participants with different levels of confidence and physical ability.

prepare teaching materials, maintain equipment and explain studio safety procedures. provide individual feedback on design choices while encouraging participants to experiment and develop their own visual language.

- facilitated more than eighty workshops for groups of six to twelve participants.
- created a short course on designing with transparent and opaque glass.
- worked with local schools to develop age-appropriate demonstrations and supervised activities.
- helped participants plan achievable projects within available firing and cooling times.

**studio assistant and glass technician**  
harbour glass studio, port adelaide  
2012–2017

assisted a team of artists with hot-shop preparation, kiln loading, mould making and finishing. maintained a clean and organised work environment and supported the safe handling of hot glass, tools and heavy materials.

recorded firing schedules, prepared materials for casting and assisted with packing finished artworks for transport. contributed to the installation of group exhibitions and commercial commissions.

- supported the fabrication of blown and kiln-cast works for local artists and visiting designers.
- improved labelling and storage procedures for glass stock, mould materials and finished components.
- assisted with equipment checks and routine maintenance under the direction of senior technicians.
- gained experience working to tight production schedules while preserving a high standard of finish.

solo exhibition, west terrace project space, adelaide  
2024

presented a collection of cast glass vessels and wall-mounted forms examining the changing colour of coastal light. the exhibition included twelve new works and an artist talk on material experimentation.

**held in the landscape**  
group exhibition, riverlands regional gallery, south australia

exhibited three layered glass panels alongside works by ceramicists, painters and textile artists. the exhibition explored personal connections to place and regional environments.

solo exhibition, north adelaide contemporary, adelaide

developed a series of translucent sculptural forms inspired by tidal movement and patterns left in sand. collaborated with a lighting designer to create an installation that changed throughout the gallery day.

**material conversations**  
group exhibition, southern craft forum, melbourne  
2018

selected to exhibit a group of hand-formed glass objects in a national survey of emerging makers working across contemporary craft disciplines.

group exhibition, adelaide

exhibited early kiln-formed works exploring repetition, translucency and the relationship between flat sheets and curved surfaces.

**selected commissions**

**coastal passage**  
corporate foyer, adelaide  
2023

designed and fabricated a set of six suspended glass elements for a reception area. worked with an engineer and installation team to resolve mounting, weight distribution and access for maintenance.

**shared horizons**  
community centre, south australia  
2021

created a wall-mounted glass artwork informed by drawings and stories contributed by local residents. facilitated three community sessions and translated recurring shapes and colours into a cohesive final design.

**morning current**  
private residence, adelaide hills  
2019

produced a pair of kiln-formed glass screens for an interior stairwell. developed samples with the clients and collaborated with a metalworker on a discreet supporting frame.

**education**

**bachelor of visual arts, glass and ceramics**  
university of south australia, adelaide  
2012

completed studio-based coursework in glass forming, material processes, contemporary art history and professional practice. final project investigated the visual effects of layering transparent glass over textured surfaces.

**advanced kiln casting intensive**  
independent studio program, canberra  
2016

completed a practical program covering mould preparation, glass selection, firing schedules and cold finishing for sculptural cast work.

**professional development and community involvement**

- participant, collaborative public art planning workshop, adelaide, 2023.
- mentor, emerging makers studio exchange, south australia, 2021–2022.
- volunteer demonstrator, community arts open day, port adelaide, 2019.

**working approach**

i enjoy projects that require close conversation between artist, client and site. i begin by listening to the people who will live with or encounter the work, then use sketches and physical samples to test ideas. i document technical decisions throughout production and communicate clearly when changes to scale, materials or timing are needed.

my studio practice also includes ongoing experiments with reclaimed glass where the material is suitable for the intended process. i keep careful records of compatibility and firing results, and i prioritise safe handling, durable construction and responsible use of materials.

*Early life and inheritance*

Raymond III was Count of Tripoli from 1152 until his death in 1187. He was a leading nobleman in the crusader states and played a major part in the politics of the Kingdom of Jerusalem. His father was Raymond II of Tripoli and his mother was Hodierna of Jerusalem. Through his mother he was related to the royal family of Jerusalem.

Raymond became count while still a child after his father was murdered. His mother helped govern the county during his minority. Tripoli occupied an important position on the eastern Mediterranean coast and its rulers had to deal with neighboring Muslim powers as well as with rival Christian princes.

*Captivity and return*

In 1164 Raymond joined other crusader leaders in a campaign against Nur al-Din. Their forces were defeated at the Battle of Harim and Raymond was captured. He spent years as a prisoner in Aleppo. His long absence weakened his ability to direct the affairs of Tripoli and left others to manage his interests.

Raymond was released in 1174 after a ransom had been arranged. He returned to a political world facing a serious challenge from Saladin. That same year King Amalric of Jerusalem died and his young son Baldwin IV succeeded him. Raymond became regent of the kingdom during the new king’s minority.

*Power in Jerusalem*

Raymond married Eschiva of Bures and gained an important position in Galilee through the marriage. His influence rested on his lands and family connections as well as on his experience in government. He favored policies that took account of the military strength of the kingdom’s Muslim neighbors.

The court of Jerusalem was divided by disputes over the succession and the influence of competing nobles. Baldwin IV suffered from leprosy and the question of who would rule after him became increasingly urgent. Raymond later served as regent for Baldwin V. After the young king died in 1186 the crown passed to Sibylla and her husband Guy of Lusignan. Raymond opposed Guy’s rise and tensions between them became severe.

*The campaign of 1187*

As Saladin prepared to invade the kingdom Raymond eventually joined forces with Guy. Saladin attacked Tiberias where Raymond’s wife was sheltering in the citadel. The crusader army marched toward the city despite Raymond’s advice against a risky advance.

Saladin’s forces defeated the crusaders at the Battle of Hattin in July 1187. Raymond led part of the Christian army and escaped from the battlefield. The defeat opened the way for Saladin to capture much of the kingdom including Jerusalem. Raymond returned to Tripoli and died later that year. His career illustrates both the political divisions within the crusader states and the mounting pressure they faced from their powerful neighbors.
